apps.notes: Official Spotify help article 'Keyboard shortcuts' (US locale), read via WebFetch and the raw HTML (curl). The page is one flat table with no section headings. Its own wording says the list is 'including (but not limited to)', so it may not be exhaustive. The example key combinations shown for Mac and Windows are images; the text table was used. The page writes 'Alt' for the Mac Option key; recorded as opt (⌥). Where the page gives 'Cmd or Ctrl', the Mac (Cmd) form is recorded and the Ctrl alternative is left out. 'Open Help' also lists Ctrl/Cmd + ? as an alternative; only the / form is recorded. Shuffle and Repeat use Alt on Mac per the page. Go to Search uses Cmd+Shift+L on Mac per the page.

apps.name: VLC media player
apps.notes: Official VideoLAN user documentation, VLC Desktop User Documentation 3.0, Hotkeys page (the 'Most Used' table). The 'Full List' section has no text; it is six images (hotkeys_one to hotkeys_six), so those hotkeys are not recorded. The page does not say which platform the 'Most Used' keys apply to, and it marks no macOS-specific entries; it calls them global hotkeys that work without VLC focus. 'ctrl + Up' and 'ctrl + Down' are recorded as written (⌃). Symbol keys + and - are recorded as written; the page does not state their Shift or numpad modifiers, so none are added. The docs.videolan.me host returned 404 for a root 3.0 path and redirected from the desktop index; the 3.0 hotkeys page loaded with curl. Not recorded: the macOS snapshot shortcut (Command+Alt+S) appears only in a third-party-referenced VideoLAN FAQ snippet, not on the hotkeys page. The wiki page wiki.videolan.org/Documentation:Hotkeys is marked as needing verification and was not used as a source.

apps.name: Dropbox

Search-result snippets from those Adobe pages mention macOS entries such as Option+Command+T (hide others) and Command+Option+W (close all open documents), but these are unverified and not recorded.
